claims.text: docker compose stop stops a service's containers; docker compose pause freezes every process in them (cgroup freezer) without closing their open TCP connections; unpause resumes them.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs 'docker compose stop', 'docker compose pause', 'docker container pause' (cgroups freezer)

claims.text: Captured stage-3 output of slow-dependency.sh: GET /api/v1/products/3 returns 200 in less than 1 s with Redis up and with Redis stopped, and 200 after more than 5 s with Redis paused.

When the Redis container stops, the client's connection breaks and StackExchange.Redis marks the endpoint as disconnected; with BacklogPolicy.FailFast a command issued meanwhile fails at once with an exception instead of being queued.
claims.source_hint: StackExchange.Redis docs 'Configuration' (BacklogPolicy), 'Connection resilience'; CatalogModule.cs @ stage-3 lines 21-27

claims.text: With the default backlog policy, StackExchange.Redis holds commands issued while disconnected and sends them once the connection is back (or fails them at their timeout); FailFast instead fails them at once.
abortConnect=false makes ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect return even when no server is reachable, and the multiplexer keeps retrying the connection in the background.
When a connection is open but the server never replies, a StackExchange.Redis command waits until its timeout and then throws RedisTimeoutException; ProductCache.IsRedisFailure treats that as a miss.
ProductCache counts any Redis failure as a cache miss and then reads PostgreSQL through the repository inside it (EfProductRepository).
ProductCache.FindAsync sends Redis more than one command per read (a GET, a second GET after the key lock, a SET after a miss), so in the paused case each of them waits for the timeout.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Catalog/ProductCache.cs lines 25-49; scripts/backend/slow-dependency.sh lines 28-30

claims.text: While an I/O call is awaited, async/await returns the thread; the request keeps its objects, the client's connection and any DB connection still open (e.g. in a transaction). EF Core (3.0+) closes its connection after each operation, so ProductCache's Redis waits hold none.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core 'Best practices' (avoid blocking calls); EF Core 3.0 breaking changes (connection closed after use); ProductCache.cs @ stage-3 lines 25-49

claims.text: A pooled database connection that a request has opened is unavailable to other requests until the request closes or disposes it.
claims.source_hint: Npgsql docs 'Connection pooling' (connection returned to the pool on Close/Dispose)

claims.text: If nothing limits how many requests of one kind run at once and they arrive faster than they finish, requests in progress pile up until a shared limit (accepted connections, DB connections, memory) runs out, and unrelated requests wait or fail too.
claims.source_hint: Google SRE book 'Addressing Cascading Failures'; Microsoft Azure Architecture Center 'Retry/Circuit Breaker pattern' (context)

claims.text: A dependency that is down usually fails at once (e.g. a refused or broken connection), while one that accepts the call but does not answer keeps the caller waiting until a timeout.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 3 and 6; foundation.l1.tcp-vs-udp (refused vs timeout)

redisConfiguration is ConnectionStrings:Redis, set in docker-compose.yml for the api as ConnectionStrings__Redis: "redis:6379,abortConnect=false" and passed to AddCatalogModule by Program.cs.

A count of requests in progress that keeps climbing while the CPU has little to do is a typical symptom of requests waiting on a slow dependency, since async/await frees only the thread.
